title.narrative: Output 7.1. Increased capacity of Member States to ensure respect for, promote and realize fundamental principles and rights at work

description.narrative: MOL strengthened the established tripartite NAP National Steering Committee (NAP NSC) that serves as national coordination mechanism to combat CL. Until August 2023, MOL held 5 general and technical meetings to review the implementation of child labour related actions. The Tripartite NAP NSC is promoting social dialogue on the elimination of child labour. On June 12, 2022, the MOL issued the Hazardous Worklist for Children Ministerial Decree 215 for 2021. The Decree was officially published in the Egyptian Gazette on the occasion of the World Day against Child Labour (WDACL). The decree sets the minimum age for employment and apprenticeship is 15 and 14 respectively. In parallel, MOL issued Ministerial Decree 78 for 2021, activated in 2022 to establish sustainable Combating Child Labour Unit to serves as a permanent mechanism concerned with coordinating national efforts to combat child labour. In addition, the Ministry of Social Solidarity (MOSS) issued Ministerial Decree 767 for 2022 to amend the Child Labour Centers (CLCs) Bylaw that was developed based on ACCEL Africa needs assessment to the 17 CLCs accross Egypt. This led to evidence-based technical recommendations and support. The bylaw provides more protection and support to working children. With the support of the Netherlands, the ILO assisted the government to take actions to eliminate child labour by reviewing and providing technical assistance on the drafting of the new ministerial decree. The ILO also helped develop the hazardous worklist for children, and provided guidance on the conduct of needs assessments and provided financial and technical assistance to strengthen the NAP NSC to conduct regular meetings and ensure national ownership, ongoing social dialogue and establish a sustainable unit to oversee eliminating child labour related issues. In addition, taking action to withdraw children from child labour and reintegrate them in education system. In addition, ensure decent transition from school to work.

Output 7.1. Increased capacity of Member States to ensure respect for, promote and realize fundamental principles and rights at work

description.narrative: Within the framework of operationalizing an integrated national BWEG Strategy (2022-2027) on FPRW focusing on the garment sector, which was validated by the tripartite constituents, the Ministry of Labour (MOL) revised the national occupational safety and health (OSH) and labour inspection compliance assessment tool/checklists in March 2022 to promote all of the FPRW. This paved the way in February 2023, to increase the capacity of 113 inspectors in on FPRW. In July 2023, MOL completed the digitalized inspection systems reflecting updated compliance assessment checklists. Additionally, in October 2022, the following significant actions were undertaken: (a) MOL issued Decree 277 for 2022 regarding Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) for Trade Union Registration to ensure transparent registration process for all. This was combined with increasing the capacities of MOL national Trade Union staff on SOPs. In addition, in January 2023, the House of Senate increased the minimum age for employment from 14 to 15 years in line with the ILO Minimum Age for Employment Convention 138 for 1973, Egyptian Constitution and MOL Decree 215 for 2021; (b) in December 2022, the Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS) completed the data collection of the National Child Labour Survey (NCLS); (c) In August 2023, the capacity of 395 tripartite constituents was increased, and awareness of 569 social women leaders was raised on combating human trafficking identification and referral of victims of trafficking. In addition, in April 2023. 25 labour inspectors were capacitated as trainers on combating human trafficking across Egypt; and (d) Gender gap analyses conducted in all BWEG enterprises on women’s participation in the workforce, supervisory roles, and leadership positions, women’s access to training opportunities and promotions to mainstream gender equity at the enterprise level. Findings were disseminated to each registered enterprises during January-March 2023. With the support of the Governments of the Netherlands, United States, Norway, and Sweden, the ILO supported the tripartite constituents to operationalize the integrated programme and promote FPRW, specifically technical expertise was mobilised to conduct analysis (e.g. gender gap analysis), workshops in and outside Cairo (e.g. OSH and labour inspection, FPRW, supervisory skills, workplace coordination and grievance mechanisms at workplace), conducting national survey (NCLS), guidance tools and SOPs (e.g. Trade Union SOPs for establishing and registering trade unions, OSH and labour checklist), provide consultations and assessment service (e.g. BWEG compliance assessment and advisory visits to enterprises, assessment and follow up field visits to MOL field inspection offices). It is worth mentioning that the ILO has increasingly utilised capacity development support with the tripartite constituents to increase sustainability and ownership.
